messages.author: a061c48a0a34b884
messages.subject: Understanding ms5.outraw
parts:
Hi all,

I am mainly interested in using GGIR to extract light information from GeneActiv watches equipped with light sensors. Specifically, I would like this information in a time series (one observation per X seconds) so I have turned on the relevant ms5.outraw parameters when calling GGIR():

save_ms5rawlevels = TRUE, # Output time series data
save_ms5raw_format = "csv",
save_ms5raw_without_invalid = TRUE

From reading the GGIR docs (Chapter 6), I understand that epoch-level ENMO is imputed using data from other days (if non-wear is detected in that epoch AND there is a sufficient number of valid days to derive the imputed value from).

Can I assume this is also the case when it comes to lux data? To be clear, I am referring to the csv files in /meta/ms5.outraw/, and the data that is found in the lightpeak column.

Thank you to everyone who has contributed to asking and answering questions on this forum so far - your discussions have been very useful!

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Understanding ms5.outraw
parts:
Hi Timothy.

Good question. It is not imputed: GGIR imputes all acceleration metrics but not temperature and lux.

I may have forgotten because my focus has been on the acceleration signals and lux and temperature are stored at a different resolution by default. That said, I am not sure what a good imputation of lux would be given that it has such a skewed distribution. Maybe a median instead of mean imputation approach would be better? I do not know the lux literature well enough to decide and would prefer if someone with expertise in this area could provide some guidance. Also, implementing this would require some effort (funding or volunteer time).

In terms practicalities: LUX is extracted in GGIR part 1, run GGIR(mode = 1, ...), and stored in object M$metalong inside the RData files a stored in subfolder meta/basic. The epoch size is modifiable with the second value of the vector as specified by parameter windowsizes. If LUX is the only aspect of GGIR you are interested in then maybe consider working with those files directly.

Best wishes,

Vincent

messages.author: a061c48a0a34b884
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Understanding ms5.outraw
parts:
Hi Vincent,

Thanks for your clarification! I agree with your point re: the skewed distribution of lux values, and decided to go ahead with median imputation for the purposes of my project.

For the benefit of others who find this, I can confirm that the lightpeak variable in M$metalong (Part 1 output) is (almost) identical to the lightpeak variable in the ms5.outraw RData files (Part 5 output). This is assuming that you have requested to  save_ms5rawlevels = TRUE and set save_ms5raw_without_invalid = TRUE.

I am also not an expert on missing data techniques, but have managed to write some code to do the median imputation. I'm happy to make this code available if others would benefit from it. Though, I agree that we will need the experts if users want more advanced imputation methods

Tim

messages.author: a061c48a0a34b884
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Understanding ms5.outraw
parts: " For the benefit of others who find this, I can confirm that the lightpeak variable in M$metalong (Part 1 output) is (almost) identical to the lightpeak variable in the ms5.outraw RData files (Part 5 output)."
They are almost identical because ms5.outraw lightpeak is the rounded form of M$metalong lightpeak, i.e. lightpeak.ms5.outraw equals round(lightpeak.metalong)
